statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-12318 is an incorrect boundary condition in NSS's PKCS#11 URI parser, fixed in Firefox 152 (https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-57/#CVE-2026-12318). The fix, Mozilla bug 2023478, changes pk11uri_ParseAttributes() in lib/util/pkcs11uri.c so that a percent escape cut short by the end of the string is rejected instead of the terminating NUL being accepted as a hex digit and the parser reading past it: https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/bd0c42028c8eae5b9cbdb4f5b0ee59bc07cba2de. The change is first in the NSS 3.124 release (the NSS_3_124_RTM tag has it, NSS_3_123_1_RTM does not). Debian backported it to trixie in 2:3.110-1+deb13u3 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-12318). The DHI Debian repository publishes three builds of nss for Debian 13: a rebuild of Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 and builds of NSS 3.131.1 and 3.132. We checked the libnss3 packages of all three on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums: the changelog shipped in the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild lists the 2:3.110-1+deb13u3 entry for CVE-2026-12318, and the libnssutil3.so version strings confirm NSS 3.110, 3.131.1 and 3.132, both of the later ones newer than 3.124. Every published build carries the fix, so the range closes at the lowest published build, the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild. Earlier 3.110 builds, from before Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u3, lack the fix and read as affected.
